Landscape 1536×1024 composition, clearly a responsive website interface—not a poster, brochure, or moodboard. Direction: “The Corridor Tile Hall,” inspired by restrained Portuguese and Southeast Asian trading-port tilework, customs halls, and wayfinding signage. Use tile logic as a modular navigation and process grammar, never as decorative wallpaper. The first viewport must prove structured company profile → organizer-reviewed match → mutual acceptance → confirmed meeting → agreement and follow-up. Exact headline: “Sharper connections for cross-border business.” Primary action: “White-label with Plexus.” Secondary: “Join as a business.” Preserve a Plexus logo area without inventing a new logo. Navigation: How it works, For vendors, For businesses, Pricing, EN / BM / 繁體中文, Login. Structure: an asymmetrical tiled corridor whose five process stations lead toward a large confirmed-meeting threshold; integrate the headline and actions into directional signage; show a human organizer review station and a pair of business profile tiles. Begin the next fold with three simple operator outcomes. Palette: cobalt #174a7e, milk white #f7f2e8, ink #17212b, aged brass #c4953d, restrained vermilion #c64a36. Materials: matte glazed ceramic, painted wayfinding enamel, fine grout lines, worn brass registration plates. Typography: disciplined contemporary sans with compact condensed labels, supporting multilingual text. The result must stay simple enough to extend into Admin: white surfaces, cobalt selection, thin tile-grid dividers. No glow, no purple, no gradients, no ornamental overload, no generic SaaS bento grid, no fake logos, no testimonials, no unverified statistics, no invented market claims.
